title: Plane Figures
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4; not yet checked by a Kenyan maths teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Outcomes a to e are KICD's words (a to d verified, e read; f attitudinal). Outcomes b (drawing) and d (patterns) are hands-on and are listed as such: they stay with paper and the teacher. The shapes are rectangles, squares, triangles, circles and ovals; lines of symmetry are found by folding.

skills.key_step: The child names rectangles, squares, triangles, circles and ovals by their sides, corners and curves, whatever way they are turned.

floor.question: A shape has three straight sides. What is it?

steps: Count the straight sides and corners.
Curved with no corners: circle or oval.
Four sides: square if all equal, rectangle if opposite sides equal.
Turning a shape does not change its name.

board.do: Draw a square standing on its corner.
Point at the sides.
board.say: Are the four sides equal and the corners square?

board.do: Wait for yes.
Write: still a square.

misconceptions.ask: Did turning it change its sides?
Is an egg the same width every way?
Does it have three straight sides?
What shape do you trace from the top?

checks.question: What shape is a one-shilling coin?
A shape has four equal sides and four square corners, standing on a corner. What is it?

skills.key_step: The child draws each shape with straight sides that meet (a ruler for rectangles, squares and triangles) and smooth closed curves for circles and ovals.

floor.question: How many sides has a rectangle?

steps: Choose the shape.
Use a ruler for straight sides.
Make the sides meet at the corners.
Curves: smooth, closed, no corners.

board.do: Draw a square with a ruler, one side at a time.
Point at a corner.
board.say: Do the two sides meet here?

board.do: Wait for yes.
The child draws a rectangle and an oval.
Check each: closed, straight sides or smooth curve.

misconceptions.ask: Are all four sides the same length?
Do all the lines meet?
misconceptions.repair: No: join them to close it.

misconceptions.ask: Does an egg have pointed ends?
Does a rectangle have square corners?

checks.question: Draw a square with sides of 4 cm. What must be true of the sides?
What must happen at every corner of a triangle you draw?

skills.key_step: The child folds a shape so the two halves fit exactly; only such folds are lines of symmetry.

floor.question: What shape has four equal sides?

steps: Fold the shape.
Do the halves fit exactly?
Yes: the fold is a line of symmetry.
Try every way: across, down and corner to corner.

board.do: Draw a rectangle and its diagonal.
Point at the diagonal.
board.say: If we fold along it, do the halves fit?

board.do: Wait for no.
Draw the two lines that do fit: down the middle and across.

misconceptions.ask: Fold a rectangle corner to corner. Do the halves fit?
Do the parts fit on top of each other?
misconceptions.repair: Only then is it a line of symmetry.

misconceptions.ask: Can you fold a circle another way and still fit?
misconceptions.repair: Yes, every way through the middle: many.

misconceptions.ask: Fold the square corner to corner. Do the halves fit?

checks.question: How many lines of symmetry has a rectangle?
How many lines of symmetry has a square?

skills.key_step: The child finds the part that repeats (shape, size, colour and the way it points) and repeats the whole part.

floor.question: Name a shape with three sides.

representations: cut-out shapes laid in a row
patterns on a kikoi or basket
steps: Find where the pattern starts again.
Mark the part that repeats.
Check shape, size, colour and direction.
Repeat the whole part.

board.do: Draw: red square, blue triangle, red square, blue triangle.
Point at the first two shapes.
Wait for red square, blue triangle.
The child draws the next two shapes.
Ring each repeat.

misconceptions.ask: What came after the last triangle before?
Look at the shape and the colour together.
What size came after a big square?
Which way did the last triangle point?
misconceptions.repair: Up, so the next points down.

checks.question: Square, square, triangle, square, square, triangle, ?
Big circle, small circle, big circle, ?

skills.key_step: The child describes each figure by its sides, corners and curves: a rectangle has opposite sides equal and four square corners; a square is a rectangle with all sides equal.

floor.question: How many corners has a rectangle?

steps: Count the sides.
Count the corners.
Check which sides are equal.
Curves: circle (same distance from the middle) or oval.

board.do: Draw a rectangle with its sides marked 6 cm and 3 cm.
Point at the opposite sides.
Wait for the opposite ones.
Mark the equal sides and the four square corners.

misconceptions.ask: Is the long side the same as the short side?
Does a square have four square corners and opposite sides equal?
misconceptions.repair: Yes: it is a rectangle too.

misconceptions.ask: Count the corners as you touch them.
Measure to the end and to the side of an oval.
misconceptions.repair: Different: only a circle is the same.

checks.question: How many sides and corners has a triangle?
Which sides of a rectangle are equal?
